candidates.prune_reason: Acute lumbar paraspinal muscle strain / myofascial pain — positive straight‑leg‑raise with distal foot radiation and acute onset during lifting make isolated muscle strain unlikely.

differential_evidence.description: MRI lumbar spine findings — presence of nerve‑root compression by a disc at a level and side that match the patient’s dermatomal pain strongly supports herniated disc; absence of compression with isolated muscle edema points toward strain or piriformis (if pelvic imaging shows piriformis enlargement).

Focused neurological exam — objective sensory deficit in a dermatomal distribution, decreased reflexes (e.g., reduced ankle jerk for S1), or motor weakness (foot dorsiflexion weakness for L5, plantarflexion for S1) favors radiculopathy; a completely normal neuro exam favors piriformis or muscle strain.

Provocative testing pattern — positive straight‑leg‑raise (and reproducible distal radicular pain) supports lumbar nerve‑root tension/radiculopathy; positive FAIR (flexion‑adduction‑internal rotation) or Freiberg test, and reproducible deep gluteal pain with hip maneuvers favor piriformis; predominantly local lumbar/paraspinal pain provoked by lumbar movement with negative neural tension tests favors muscle strain.

Diagnostic procedures/EMG — immediate pain relief after a targeted piriformis injection supports piriformis syndrome; EMG/NCS showing active denervation in a myotomal distribution supports radiculopathy (useful if MRI is inconclusive); lack of electrophysiologic abnormalities plus local tender trigger points favors muscle strain.
